title: Atlas Rover — Q3 firmware planning
note: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — fictional company (Helios Dynamics), fictional people, generated for benchmark use. No real meeting data.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Alright, let's start the Q3 firmware planning for the Atlas rover line. Agenda is the motor controller refactor, the OTA update pipeline, and staffing.

segments.speaker: Jonas Pike
segments.text: Quick status first: the v2.3 firmware is stable in the field, but we still see the encoder drift bug on about two percent of units.

segments.speaker: Ines Calder
segments.text: The drift correlates with the cheaper encoder batch from the Tessier supplier. Software can compensate, but it costs us control-loop headroom.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Is the compensation shippable in Q3 or do we push the supplier?

segments.speaker: Ines Calder
segments.text: Compensation is two weeks of work. Pushing the supplier is a six-month contract discussion. I recommend we ship the software compensation now and open the supplier discussion in parallel.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Agreed. Decision: we ship the encoder drift compensation in firmware v2.4, and Ravi opens the supplier quality discussion with Tessier.

segments.speaker: Ravi Mehta
segments.text: I'll draft the quality addendum and send it to Tessier by next Friday.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Next topic: the motor controller refactor. Jonas, where are we?

segments.speaker: Jonas Pike
segments.text: The refactor splits the monolithic control task into three RTOS tasks: sensing, control law, and actuation. Prototype runs on the bench rig, but I haven't profiled worst-case latency yet.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: What's the risk if latency regresses?

segments.speaker: Jonas Pike
segments.text: If the actuation task misses its one-millisecond deadline, the rover stutters on slopes. I want a hard latency budget test in CI before we merge.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Good. Decision: the motor controller refactor merges only after a CI latency budget test exists and passes. Jonas owns the test, due end of June.

segments.speaker: Jonas Pike
segments.text: Works for me. I'll need the second bench rig from the Hamburg lab for the profiling runs.

segments.speaker: Ravi Mehta
segments.text: I can arrange the rig transfer. Logistics take about a week, so I'll book it today.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: On to OTA updates. Ines, you flagged a security concern last week.

segments.speaker: Ines Calder
segments.text: Yes. The current OTA pipeline verifies the image signature only at download time, not at boot. A corrupted flash write could brick a unit or, worse, boot unsigned code.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: That sounds like a must-fix before we scale the fleet.

segments.speaker: Ines Calder
segments.text: It is. I propose secure boot verification in the bootloader for v2.4. It's about three weeks, including the key provisioning ceremony for the factory.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Decision: secure boot verification ships in v2.4 ahead of the fleet scale-up. Ines owns it. The key provisioning ceremony needs a written runbook — Ines, please draft it by July 10th.

segments.speaker: Ines Calder
segments.text: Understood. Draft runbook by July 10th.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Last item: staffing. We have one open embedded role. Jonas, you mentioned a candidate?

segments.speaker: Jonas Pike
segments.text: Yes, a strong candidate from the Bremen robotics group. I'd like Ines in the final interview loop for the security angle.

segments.speaker: Ines Calder
segments.text: Happy to. Schedule it any afternoon next week.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: Ravi, please coordinate the interview loop with recruiting for next week.

segments.speaker: Ravi Mehta
segments.text: Will do, I'll set it up with recruiting tomorrow morning.

segments.speaker: Mara Voss
segments.text: To summarize: v2.4 carries the encoder drift compensation and secure boot. The motor refactor lands behind the CI latency gate. Supplier talks and the interview loop start this week. Thanks everyone.
